subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar, and if so should the contract be markdown sidecar, structured skill config, or no core support?
rationale: Source evidence shows the requested behavior is missing, but adding it changes a public skill-loading and prompt-context contract rather than repairing an already-defined bug.

options.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
options.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that is loaded with the selected skill, lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, and included in prompt-version, watcher, and security behavior.

options.title: Use structured skill config
options.body: Keep preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require each skill or plugin to interpret them, avoiding markdown prompt composition while making natural-language conventions less ergonomic.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the current model of full skill overrides, custom skills, or global context files, and close this direction as not planned if maintainers do not want another skill-loading surface.

recommendation.title: Standardize a markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that is loaded with the selected skill, lower precedence than `SKILL.md`, and included in prompt-version, watcher, and security behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history signal for grouped skill loading, skill docs, and skill config API decisions points to steipete.
